dedupe_keys.name: combining active and passive temperature signals for estimating sediment depths

description: Regueiro-Picallo, Manuel at Universidade da Coruña publishes measurements of sediment thermal properties and temperature-based deposit depths through Co-UDlabs. The Langeveld transnational-access campaign develops an active temperature-sensing system and adds sensors at several heights. The purpose is to characterise urban-drainage sediments and evaluate accumulation inference from active and passive thermal signals. Coverage is the Eawag HALL experimental campaign in Switzerland; exact dates and sensor spacing are unspecified. Zenodo provides a data ZIP and a PDF campaign report with free access under CC BY-NC 4.0. These observations support the source-defined drainage measurement, physical-model or simulation activity. Related Co-UDlabs experiments describe other assets and test conditions; they are not assumed to be independent or interchangeable measurements. A limitation is measured thermal properties and temperature responses are material-dependent, and the inspected metadata do not give all calibration coefficients. Only native metadata and file descriptors were read; no data values, archive, code or report body was obtained.
